summary: Basankusu territory (Equateur) is a remote forested territory on the Lulonga/Maringa/Lopori rivers with no reported armed-group presence as of late 2026. Armed conflict records for Basankusu and Djombo date from the 1999-2002 war, when the MLC took the area. The state controls the territory through the territorial administration and the PNC, with a small FARDC presence in Basankusu town. All locations in the Basankusu and Djombo secteurs are assessed as default PNC control, with low confidence for rural villages.

sources.title: MLC atrocities near Basankusu, Djombo and Kodoro (2000)

zones.description: Basankusu town (territorial seat, river port at Lulonga/Maringa/Lopori confluence) and adjacent Ikau
zones.evidence: Basankusu is the territorial headquarters with territorial administration, PNC commissariat and a small FARDC presence. Searches (FR/EN, 2025-2026) found no reports of armed groups, militias or rebel activity in Basankusu territory; conflict records for Basankusu and Djombo date from the 1999-2002 war (MLC vs FAC). The territory is remote forest in Equateur, far from eastern conflict zones and the Mobondo area; state authority via territorial administration and PNC is assumed.

zones.description: Basankusu secteur villages (Lisafa, Ndeke, Ilodze, Bongilima, Nsongo Nkoy, Bokakata, Lilangi, Monzonzo health areas)
zones.evidence: Searches (FR/EN, 2025-2026) found no reports of armed groups, militias or rebel activity in Basankusu territory; conflict records for Basankusu and Djombo date from the 1999-2002 war (MLC vs FAC). Police presence in remote villages is thin; customary chiefs handle most disputes.

zones.description: Djombo secteur villages (Djombo health zone: Djombo, Boso Ngwanza, Bobambo, Bosongo, Boso Maswa, Kodoro areas)
